additionalCoursework: SIU School of Medicine lists courses we "recommend" but not "require" in order to apply to our medical school.  We list all of those courses here:  https://www.siumed.edu/studentaffairs/requirements-selection-factors-and-policies

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: An active effort is made to recruit qualified applicants from all backgrounds. For more information, contact the Office of Diversity at 217 545 7334. The School of Medicine also sponsors the Medical/Dental Education Preparatory Program (MEDPREP), a non-degree granting program in Carbondale for disadvantaged undergraduate or postbaccalaureate students, as well as underrepresented, rural, or low-income students (http://www.siumed.edu/medprep/ ).
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student may request a Leave of Absence from the Associate Dean for Student Affairs or designee. The request must be in writing and must set out the dates and reasons therefore and the proposed use of Leave of Absence time. The Associate Dean for Student Affairs or designee may grant the request or refer the request to the Student Progress Committee for action.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: School of Medicine students area active in a wide range of extracurricular pursuits on both campuses. They participate in local chapters of national organizations and advocate for student interests as members of student government bodies and faculty committees. Special interest groups for medical specialties provide forums and activities for those with specific practice goals. SIU medical students are active in service projects such as mentoring and donating time to public health awareness and screening initiatives. For those interested in scientific research, the school offers a medical student research program and provides opportunities for presentation and publication of results.  Springfield and Carbondale offer numerous opportunities for recreation and entertainment. The area surrounding Carbondale is noted for its physical beauty and for exceptional outdoor activities including hiking, camping, kayaking, rock climbing, etc. Springfield and Carbondale also offer many other enterta
medSchoolStudLife.setting: SIU School of Medicine holds the first year of medical school in a small-town, collegiate environment at SIU-Carbondale, an institution serving over 20,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. The remaining three years take place at the SIU medical campus in Springfield (pop. 115,000), the state capital. The facilities in Springfield are located in one of downstate Illinois' largest and fastest growing medical districts.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Carbondale and Springfield: off-campus housing. Monthly rates for apartments in both locations: $450 to $600 per month.

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: SIU SOM is known for having a collaborative, student-centered campus with a strong emphasis on serving the health-care needs of Central/Southern Illinois.  We have small class sizes that foster close relationships between students, faculty and staff.  We are innovative and hands-on with our medical school education and have a very mission-driven culture, collaborative, not competitive environment and have strong community engagement.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: All students live off-campus so transportation is highly recommended.

Also, peer tutors available.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The overall focus of the first two years of the curriculum is on case-based, student-directed learning in a small-group setting supported by lectures/resource sessions. Close integration of basic science and clinical information takes place throughout the four-year course of study. Clinical training begins in the first year with real and simulated patients. An increased emphasis on issues such as community health care and the psychosocial issues of medicine continues SIU School of Medicine's emphasis on caring while curing and treating patients as people rather than medical conditions. The third year consists of a series of multidisciplinary clinical rotations, with emphasis on both hospital-based and ambulatory practice. The fourth year comprises a series of electives designed to help students with final preparations for residency. The grading system is honors/pass/fail.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: SIU School of Medicine historically places a relatively large number of its graduates into primary care careers upon graduation. Since 1981, the school has offered and required a family and community medicine rotation for third-year medical students. This program made SIU one of the earliest medical schools in the country to engage students in community- based education, placing students in ambulatory care settings with practicing physicians.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Physicians and research scientists at the school of medicine are currently working on over 250 active research projects. These projects represent research in many areas including biomedical sciences, patient safety, and medical education. The school has notable accomplishments in the areas of medical education, neuroscience, aging and cancer.   Research opportunities exist for medical students beginning after the first year of medical school. Mentored Professional Enrichment Experiences (MPEE) take place with SIU and non-SIU faculty and these projects and others can be continued throughout the remainder of medical school.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Southern Illinois University School of Medicine was established in 1969 and graduated its first class in 1975. Students spend the first 12 months of the program at the medical education facilities on the Carbondale campus and the remaining three years at the Medical Center in Springfield.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the SIU School of Medicine is to optimize the health of the people of central and southern Illinois through education, patient care, research and service to the community.  With a Vision of Better health for all.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Require FOUR total letters OR ONE Committee Letter.

If submitting four individual letters,  at least three of them MUST be from an academic source.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Welcome Session with Director of Admissions; Two, one-on-one Interviews;  Financial Aid Session; Tour with a current medical student.

medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: MD: two one-on-one interviews; MD/JD: three one-on-one interviews.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We see all MCAT scores but use the MOST RECENT MCAT Score.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Minimum MCAT we will allow is a 498
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo:
Minimum GPA (both science and total) 2.80
With focus on the most recent 60 hours of coursework.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We require at least 90 semester hours of undergraduate work from an accredited US or Canadian degree-granting college or university.  Preference is given to those who will have earned a baccalaureate degree and who have sufficient recent academic activity to demonstrate their potential for success. Applicants with foreign credits must have completed at least 60 semester hours of coursework in the United States.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
We will accept community college coursework, however, the upper level science courses we recommend would require attending an undergraduate/graduate institution.
While we do not require a bachelor's degree in order to apply, 100% of our matriculants have obtained a bachelors degree.  We do require at least 90 semester hours of undergraduate work from an accredited US or Canadian Degree-Granting college or University.  Preference is given to those  who have earned a bachelor's degree.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We will accept updates to an applicants file.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The School participates in all major federal student aid programs. Students receive aid on the basis of need as calculated on the FAFSA. Scholarship and grant aid are generally limited to students who demonstrate exceptional need.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition costs are reviewed annually by the Southern Illinois University Board of Trustees.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: SIU School of Medicine does not have any premedical coursework requirements, but  highly recommends the following coursework be completed:  1 year general biology, 2 years of chemistry (including organic chemistry), 1 year of English composition, 1 year general physics, 1 year of math, including statistics, 1 semester of biochemistry, cell/molecular biology, physiology, genetics
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have prerequisite coursework requirements, we only list courses we recommend.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applications for the M.D. program are accepted from Illinois residents who are U.S. citizens or possess a permanent resident visa. Completion of a minimum of 90 semester hours of undergraduate work in an accredited degree-granting college or university is required. Applicants with an international education are advised to have completed at least 60 semester hours of coursework in the United States. The M.D.-J.D. program is open to non-Illinois residents. All applicants are expected to have a strong foundation in the natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities; and they must demonstrate facility in writing and speaking the English language. Preference is given to those with sufficient recent academic activity to demonstrate the potential for successful completion of the rigorous educational program and to those who demonstrate the necessary noncognitive characteristics of a successful medical student and physician. Applicants are invited for interviews according to their strengths
